newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Caemi to focus on iron ore.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Caemi to focus on iron ore.

text.p: Brazil's Caemi Mineracao e Metalurgia SA aims to return to profit by focusing on its own iron ore business after failing in its bid for CVRD, the sprawling mining concern that was recently privatized.
"We plan to focus investment in iron ore," Caemi Chairman Guilherme Frering told reporters on Thursday.
Earlier, Brazil's second-largest iron miner posted a loss of 11.31 million reais in the first half of 1997, compared with a loss of 26.54 million reais in the same period of 1996.

Caemi was part of a consortium led by industrial group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo American that narrowly failed in its bid to buy CVRD, or Cia Vale do Rio Doce, in May. The group was outbid in the privatization auction by a consortium led by Brazil's Cia Siderurgica Nacional.

Caemi plans to finance part of its investments via a $180 million capital injection from Japan's Mitsui & Co, which earlier this year bought a 40 percent stake in the company, Caemi Market Relations Director Samir Zraick said.

As part of a strategy of focusing on larger projects, Caemi has sold its chrome ore mine in Amapa in northeastern Brazil to Norway's Elkem ASA, and last year stopped manganese ferroally production in the same region, Frering said.

Caemi succeeded in turning around its MBR iron-ore mining operation and acquired a 30 percent participation on a 30-year lease to operate of the railway network linking MBR's mines near Belo Horizonte to its private terminal south of Rio de Janeiro.
MBR showed an adjusted net profit of 7.9 million reais in the first half compared with a loss of 5.5 million reais in the same period in 1996.
"We obtained significant gains and a greater reliability in ensuring transport," said Frering.

MBR was expected to sell 26.0 million tonnes of iron ore in 1997, up from 23.5 million tonnes the previous year. Of the total forecast, 23.0 million tonnes were for export and 3.0 million tonnes for the domestic market, Caemi figures showed.
MBR sold 11.95 million tonnes of iron ore in the first half. Europe was the largest customer, buying 33 percent, followed by Southeast Asia with 22 percent and Japan with 20 percent.
China, Korea and Taiwan are likely to emerge as major iron ore buyers over the next few years, Zraick said.
Caemi operates four companies - MBR, Canadian iron ore company Quebec Cartier Mining (QCM), paper coating materials producers Caulin da Amazonia and Para Pigmentos, and Brazilian bauxite miner MSL.
